mainTopic: Blood found in urine, and blood stains on a lent or shared garment or bench
overview: The משנה starts with a woman who sees blood while urinating. רבי מאיר says she is טמאה if she was standing and טהורה if she was sitting, while רבי יוסי says she is טהורה either way. When a man and a woman urinated into the same basin, רבי יוסי rules her טהורה, and רבי שמעון rules her טמאה, because blood is presumed to come from the woman. The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's split between standing and sitting with the cases of a strong stream and of sitting on the edge of the basin. It then rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about whether רבי מאיר is strict even with a ספק ספקא, and a ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן that he is not. Two more questions show that רבי שמעון is strict in every case, sitting or standing, even with a man present. A new משנה then teaches about blood stains on a garment lent to a נכרית or a נדה, or shared by three women, and רבי נחמיה's rule that items which cannot become impure do not carry stains. The גמרא begins with רב explaining the case of the נכרית, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Blood seen while urinating: standing versus sitting
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about a woman who sees blood while urinating. רבי מאיר makes it depend on her position. רבי יוסי says she is always טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who was urinating and saw blood: רבי מאיר says if she was standing she is impure, and if she was sitting she is pure. רבי יוסי says either way she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a case of blood mixed with urine and gives two opinions about whether the woman becomes טמאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the blood came from the מקור (the uterus), which makes her טמאה, or from a wound in the urinary tract, which does not. רבי מאיר thinks her position changes how likely it is that the blood came from the מקור. רבי יוסי treats her as טהורה in both positions.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'doing her needs'; here it means urinating

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman who is urinating
and she saw blood,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אִם עוֹמֶדֶת — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: if she is standing, she is impure,
and if she is sitting, she is pure.
Rabbi Yosei says:
whether this way or that way, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא עוֹשָׂה צְרָכֶיהָ וְרָאֲתָה דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: standing makes her טמאה and sitting leaves her טהורה. רבי יוסי: she is טהורה in both positions.

steps.title: Blood found in a basin used by a man and a woman
steps.stepSummary: A man and a woman both urinated into one basin and blood is found on the water. רבי יוסי rules her טהורה. רבי שמעון rules her טמאה, because blood is presumed to come from the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man and a woman urinated into a basin and blood was found on the water. רבי יוסי says she is pure. רבי שמעון says she is impure, because men do not normally pass blood, so we assume the blood came from the woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case, where it is not even clear whose blood it is, and records a new מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי already said she is טהורה when the blood is surely hers. Here there is an added doubt about whether it is hers at all, so he certainly rules טהורה. רבי שמעון says that doubt does not really count, since men do not usually pass blood. That leaves the blood presumed to be hers, so she is טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The presumption about where the blood came from

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's reason is a חזקה: men do not usually pass blood, so blood is presumed to be the woman's.

phrases.aramaic: אִישׁ וְאִשָּׁה שֶׁעָשׂוּ צׇרְכֵיהֶן לְתוֹךְ הַסֵּפֶל,
phrases.english: A man and a woman who urinated into the basin,
and blood was found on the water:
Rabbi Yosei rules her pure,
and Rabbi Shimon rules her impure,
because it is not a man's way to pass blood,
rather, blood is presumed to come from the woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישׁ וְאִשָּׁה שֶׁעָשׂוּ צׇרְכֵיהֶן לְתוֹךְ הַסֵּפֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה that adds a doubt about whose blood it is
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: טהורה. רבי שמעון: טמאה, because blood is presumed to be the woman's.

steps.title: Why should sitting be different from standing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about רבי מאיר's view. If standing makes us worry that urine went back to the מקור and brought out blood, the same worry should apply when she sits.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about standing, that we say the urine went back to the uterus and brought out blood? When she is sitting, let us also say the urine went back to the uterus and brought out blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's split between standing and sitting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא first states the reason a standing woman is טמאה: the urine may have flowed back into the מקור and carried uterine blood out with it. It then argues that nothing in this reason depends on standing. So a sitting woman should be טמאה too.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What is different? (asks why two cases are treated differently)
The uterus, the source of נדה blood

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is different about standing,
that we say:
the urine went back to the uterus
and brought out blood?
When she is sitting too, let us say:

phrases.aramaic: מֵי רַגְלַיִם הֲדוּר לְמָקוֹר וְאַיְיתִי דָּם!
phrases.english: the urine went back to the uterus and brought out blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי מאיר's ruling from step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's distinction between standing and sitting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for impurity (urine returning to the מקור) seems to apply just as much when she sits.

steps.title: שמואל: the case is a strong stream
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the משנה is talking about urine that comes out in a strong, steady stream.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: we are talking about urine that shoots out in a strong stream.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question from step 3 by narrowing the case the משנה is describing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a sitting woman's urine flows out in a strong stream, it does not flow back into the מקור, so the blood is not assumed to come from there. When she stands, the urine does not flow so smoothly, and it can flow back and bring out uterine blood. That is why only standing makes her טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shoots out, flows in a strong stream

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
It is where it shoots out in a stream.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Urine could flow back to the מקור in both positions.
steps.terutzMaskana: A strong stream while sitting does not flow back to the מקור, so only standing raises the worry.

steps.title: Even with a strong stream, blood may come afterward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל. Even if the urine flowed out in a stream, blood from the מקור may have come out right after the urine ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even with a strong stream, maybe after the urine finished, blood came out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's answer by raising a new way the blood could have come from the מקור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל removed the worry that urine flowed back into the מקור. But the blood may still be uterine blood that came out on its own once the urine stopped. If so, a sitting woman should also be טמאה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a new worry, not the same one as step 3. There the concern was urine flowing back into the מקור. Here it is blood coming out on its own after the urine ends.

phrases.english: Even when it shoots out in a stream,
perhaps after the water had finished
blood came out?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְזַנֶּקֶת נָמֵי, דִּלְמָא בָּתַר דְּתַמּוּ מַיָּא אֲתָא דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation that the משנה speaks of a strong stream
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even without urine flowing back, blood from the מקור could come out on its own after the urine stops, so a sitting woman should also be טמאה.

steps.title: Blood inside the basin came with the stream, not after it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers the challenge to שמואל. The woman sat on the edge of the basin and shot her stream into it. Blood that came after the stream ended would have landed on the edge, not inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: The case is where she sits on the edge of the basin and shoots her urine into the middle of the basin, and the blood is found inside the basin. If the blood had come after the urine stopped, it would have been found on the edge of the basin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 5 by describing exactly how the woman was sitting and where the blood landed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that blood from the מקור might have dripped out just after the urine ended. When she sits on the rim, anything that dribbles out after the stream stops falls on the rim, not into the middle. So blood found inside the basin must have traveled with the strong stream, and the worry goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: shoots out in a strong, forceful stream

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
It is where she sits on the edge of the basin,
and shoots her stream into the basin,
and blood is found inside the basin,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם אִיתָא דְּבָתַר דְּתַמּוּ מַיָּא אֲתָא
phrases.english: for if it were so that it came after the urine finished,

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׂפַת הַסֵּפֶל אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְאִשְׁתְּכוֹחֵי.
phrases.english: it should have been found on the edge of the basin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: בְּיוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל שְׂפַת הַסֵּפֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 by narrowing the case even further.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a specific way of sitting and a specific place where the blood was found.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought blood could have dripped out right after the stream ended and still be mixed into the basin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood that comes after the stream would land on the rim. Blood found inside the basin came with the urine.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who says she is טהורה. רבי אבא gave the same ruling to קלא.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said (and some say רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל): The הלכה is like רבי יוסי. רבי אבא also ruled for קלא that the הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling for the משנה's מחלוקת: we follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי held that a woman who sees blood while urinating is טהורה in every position. This ruling settles the question in practice, so we do not follow רבי מאיר's distinction between sitting and standing. A second sage, רבי אבא, ruled the same way, which strengthens the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the practical law follows this opinion
he ruled (gave a practical הלכה ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי: blood seen while urinating does not make her טמאה, whether she is sitting or standing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a debate in the משנה into practical הלכה for a woman who finds blood in her urine.

phrases.english: Shmuel said, and some say
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אוֹרִי לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְקָלָא
phrases.english: and similarly Rabbi Abba ruled for Kala
phrases.notes: קלא is the name of a sage who asked רבי אבא about this case.

phrases.english: that the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of רבי מאיר's view, the גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the first case in the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: she is טהורה.

steps.title: What would רבי מאיר say if the man and woman were both standing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second case in the משנה, where a man and a woman both urinated into one basin. It asks how רבי מאיר would rule if both of them were standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "A man and a woman, etc." A question was asked: if a man and a woman were standing, what would רבי מאיר say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the משנה's second case. This step sets up the question, and the next step explains its two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said that a woman who sees blood while standing is טמאה. In the basin case, though, the blood might even have come from the man. The question is whether רבי מאיר's strict ruling still applies when the source of the blood is less clear.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised before them (an open question the sages asked)

phrases.english: "A man and a woman, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה's case from step 2: both urinated into one basin and blood was found.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If a man and a woman were standing,
what would Rabbi Meir say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first case in the משנה, which was just settled, to the second case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי מאיר, who is strict when she is standing, would rule when a man and a woman were both standing and urinated into one basin.

steps.title: Single doubt or double doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out both sides of the question. Maybe רבי מאיר is strict only when there is one doubt and not when there is a double doubt. Or maybe it makes no difference to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי מאיר said she is טמאה, maybe that was only where there is one doubt, but where there is a double doubt he would not call her טמאה. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the question in step 8 really depends on: does רבי מאיר still say טמאה when there are two doubts instead of one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a woman alone, there is one doubt: did the blood come from a wound or from the מקור? With a man also there, there are two doubts: did the blood come from him or from her, and if from her, was it from a wound or from the מקור? This step lays out both possibilities, and the next steps give two answers: ריש לקיש in step 10 and רבי יוחנן in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: a double doubt (a doubt on top of a doubt)

steps.confusionAlert: The two doubts are separate questions: (1) from the man or from the woman, and (2) if from the woman, from a wound or from the מקור. Together they make a ספק ספקא.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּחַד סְפֵקָא,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Meir said she is impure, that was where there is one doubt,
phrases.notes: The one doubt is whether the blood came from a wound or from the מקור.

phrases.english: but in a double doubt he does not rule her impure,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּחַד סְפֵקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the question in step 8 by laying out its two sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר's strict ruling applies only to a single doubt, or to a ספק ספקא as well.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: No difference for רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that רבי מאיר rules the same way in the double-doubt case. His proof is that the משנה does not list רבי מאיר alongside רבי יוסי as being lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: It is the same. How do we know? Because the משנה does not say, 'רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי rule she is pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question from Steps 8 and 9. He says רבי מאיר is strict even when there is a double doubt, and he proves it from how the משנה is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case of the משנה, only רבי יוסי is quoted as saying טהורה. If רבי מאיר agreed there, the משנה would have said 'רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי rule she is pure.' Since it does not, רבי מאיר must still say טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the same thing. Here: the double-doubt case is the same as the single-doubt case.
From what? How do we know?
Since it does not teach. This is a proof from what the משנה leaves out.
A double doubt: two separate uncertainties stacked together.

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the מחלוקת between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן. Both of them build on the exact wording of the משנה.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: It is the same.
phrases.notes: He means רבי מאיר rules the double-doubt case exactly like the single-doubt case.

phrases.english: From where do we know? From the fact that it does not teach:
'Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei deem her pure.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Steps 8 and 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר says טמאה even in a ספק ספקא, as shown by the משנה naming only רבי יוסי as lenient.

steps.title: Why teach the single-doubt case at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: if רבי מאיר is strict even with a double doubt, then of course he is strict with one doubt. Why does the משנה need to tell us that?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, now that רבי מאיר says impure in a double doubt, is it necessary to say it in a single doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's view. It says that his reading makes the first case in the משנה seem unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A double doubt is a stronger reason to be lenient than a single doubt. So if רבי מאיר is strict even in the double-doubt case, his strictness in the single-doubt case is obvious. The משנה should not need to state it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. This introduces a challenge built on the view just stated.
Now, i.e., since this is true...
Is it necessary? Isn't it obvious?

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא רַבִּי מֵאִיר בִּסְפֵק סְפֵקָא מְטַמֵּא,
phrases.english: now that Rabbi Meir deems her impure in a case of compound uncertainty,
is it necessary to teach it in a case of one uncertainty?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַשְׁתָּא רַבִּי מֵאִיר בִּסְפֵק סְפֵקָא מְטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading of רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר is strict in the harder case, stating his view in the easier case is superfluous.

steps.title: To show how far רבי יוסי goes
steps.stepSummary: The single-doubt case is taught to show the strength of רבי יוסי's view. He says טהורה even when there is only one doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is to show you the strength of רבי יוסי, who says pure even in a single doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש. The first case is not there for רבי מאיר's sake but for רבי יוסי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being lenient with only one doubt is a bold position. By placing the argument in the single-doubt case, the משנה shows how far רבי יוסי is willing to go.

keyTerms.meaning: To let you know his strength, i.e., how far-reaching his opinion is.

phrases.english: To convey the far-reaching nature of the opinion of Rabbi Yosei,
that he deems her pure even in a case of one uncertainty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the purpose of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The single-doubt case is redundant according to ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is there to show the strength of רבי יוסי's lenient view.

steps.title: Why not show רבי מאיר's strength instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: instead of setting the argument in the single doubt to show רבי יוסי's strength, the משנה could set it in the double doubt to show רבי מאיר's strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather than arguing about a single doubt to show רבי יוסי's strength, let them argue about a double doubt to show רבי מאיר's strength!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 12. It points out that the משנה could just as easily have highlighted רבי מאיר's strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case highlights a different sage. A single doubt shows how lenient רבי יוסי is, and a double doubt would show how strict רבי מאיר is. So why did the משנה choose רבי יוסי's side?

phrases.english: But rather than disputing in a case of one uncertainty,
to convey the far-reaching nature of the opinion of Rabbi Yosei,
let them dispute in a case of compound uncertainty,
to convey the far-reaching nature of the opinion of Rabbi Meir!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the משנה wanted to show רבי יוסי's strength
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה could equally have shown רבי מאיר's strength, so why prefer רבי יוסי's?

steps.title: Showing the strength of a lenient view is preferred
steps.stepSummary: The תנא prefers to show the strength of the lenient opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The strength of a lenient ruling is preferable to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a תנא would rather highlight how far a lenient view goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being strict is easy to say even when one is unsure. Being lenient takes confidence. So showing the reach of a leniency teaches more, and the משנה chose רבי יוסי's side.

keyTerms.meaning: The strength of a permitting (lenient) view is preferable to teach.

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, רבי מאיר is strict even in a ספק ספקא. The משנה set the argument in the single doubt only to show how far רבי יוסי's leniency goes, because כֹּחַ דְּהֶיתֵּרָא עֲדִיף.
steps.whyThisMatters: כֹּחַ דְּהֶיתֵּרָא עֲדִיף is a general principle used across ש״ס to explain why a משנה chose one case over another.

phrases.english: The strength of a lenient ruling is preferable to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the תנא who wrote the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 and closes ריש לקיש's line.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle of how a משנה is taught
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both choices are equal, so the choice of the single doubt seems arbitrary.
steps.terutzMaskana: A תנא prefers to show the reach of a lenient view.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: רבי מאיר is strict only with one doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש. רבי מאיר says טמאה only in a single doubt, not in a double doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: When רבי מאיר spoke, it was about a single doubt. But about a double doubt he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the other answer to the question from Steps 8 and 9. In his view, רבי מאיר agrees she is pure when both a man and a woman urinated into the basin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the two sides of the question in Step 9 split. ריש לקיש took the side that it makes no difference to רבי מאיר. רבי יוחנן takes the side that רבי מאיר is strict only with one doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: When he said it, i.e., his statement applies only to...

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּחַד סְפֵקָא,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Meir says she is impure, that is in a case of one uncertainty,
but in a case of compound uncertainty he did not say so.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּחַד סְפֵקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש (Step 10).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר is strict only in a single doubt, not in a ספק ספקא.

steps.title: Then the משנה should name רבי מאיר too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: if רבי מאיר agrees she is pure in the double-doubt case, the משנה should say 'רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי rule she is pure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it teach: 'רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי rule she is pure'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns ריש לקיש's proof from Step 10 into a challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names only רבי יוסי in the second case. If רבי מאיר also says טהורה there, leaving him out is strange.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. This introduces a challenge built on the view just stated.
Let it teach, i.e., the משנה should have said...

phrases.english: If so,
let it teach: 'Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei deem her pure'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר agrees she is pure, the משנה should have named him together with רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The משנה just continued with רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר really does agree. The משנה named only רבי יוסי because the previous clause ended with רבי יוסי, so the new clause opened with him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But since the משנה ended with רבי יוסי, it opened with רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. Leaving out רבי מאיר is just a matter of how the משנה flows, not a sign that he disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause of the משנה ends with רבי יוסי's view. The second clause simply picks up from where the משנה left off, so it mentions רבי יוסי alone. ריש לקיש's proof from the wording is therefore not decisive.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so. This admits the point.
Since; because of the flow of the text.
That it finished, or left off.

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: רבי מאיר says טמאה even in a ספק ספקא. רבי יוחנן: רבי מאיר says טמאה only in a single doubt. The משנה names only רבי יוסי in the second case because it just continued from where the first clause ended.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
phrases.notes: He admits that רבי מאיר really does agree she is pure here.

phrases.english: but since it left off with Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: The first case in the משנה ends with רבי יוסי's view.

phrases.english: it opened with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, וְאַיְּידֵי דְּסָלֵיק מֵרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic explanation of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out רבי מאיר shows that he disagrees.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר is left out only because the משנה continued from רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Why teach רבי יוסי's leniency in the double doubt?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוסי rules her pure with only one doubt, it is obvious he rules her pure with two doubts. So why does the משנה bother to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוסי already rules her pure when there is only one doubt. Do we really need to be told he rules her pure when there are two doubts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to state רבי יוסי's lenient view in the man-and-woman case at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier clause, a woman alone, רבי יוסי rules her pure even though there is only one doubt: the blood came either from a wound or from the womb. The man-and-woman case adds a second doubt, because the blood may have come from the man. If he is lenient with one doubt, he is surely lenient with two, so teaching it looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A double doubt, a doubt on top of a doubt
Is it needed? (meaning: it is obvious)

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yosei rules her pure even with one doubt,
is it necessary to say it in a double doubt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 17 explained why the משנה names רבי יוסי first. Now the גמרא asks why his opinion needs to be taught at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to state רבי יוסי's ruling in the double-doubt case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if he is lenient with one doubt, he is certainly lenient with two, so the statement looks unnecessary.

steps.title: Even from the start, not only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought רבי יוסי is lenient only after she already touched pure things. The משנה teaches that he is lenient even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: his leniency works only after the fact, but not from the start. So the משנה teaches us that he is lenient even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the double-doubt case teaches something new: רבי יוסי rules her pure even לכתחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the single-doubt case alone, we might have limited רבי יוסי's leniency to בדיעבד, meaning she already touched pure items and we do not make them impure. The double-doubt case shows that his leniency applies לכתחילה too, so she may handle pure items from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken assumption the text corrects)
After the fact, once it already happened
So it teaches us (the new point)

phrases.english: You might have said:
this ruling applies only after the fact,
but not from the start,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a new point (a חידוש) in the extra case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי is lenient only בדיעבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי rules her pure even לכתחילה.
steps.whatToRemember: The double-doubt case is not extra. It teaches that רבי יוסי's leniency applies לכתחילה, not only בדיעבד.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that in the man-and-woman case, both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי rule her pure, just as רבי יוחנן said.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רבי יוחנן: a man and a woman urinated into a basin and blood was found on the water. רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי rule her pure, and רבי שמעון rules her impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that openly names רבי מאיר as ruling her pure in the double-doubt case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said רבי מאיר rules her טמאה even in a ספק ספקא. רבי יוחנן said רבי מאיר is strict only in a single doubt. This ברייתא lists רבי מאיר together with רבי יוסי as ruling her pure, which proves רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: In agreement with him, supporting his view
Their needs (a polite way of saying they urinated)

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in agreement with Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: אִישׁ וְאִשָּׁה שֶׁעָשׂוּ צׇרְכֵיהֶן לְתוֹךְ הַסֵּפֶל,
phrases.english: A man and a woman who urinated into a basin,
and blood was found on the water,
Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei rule her pure,
and Rabbi Shimon rules her impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן debate with an outside source backing רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי מאיר rules her pure in a ספק ספקא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that names רבי מאיר alongside רבי יוסי as ruling her pure
steps.whatToRemember: In the man-and-woman case, רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי rule her pure, and only רבי שמעון rules her טמאה. This matches רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Does רבי שמעון rule a sitting woman impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי שמעון's strict ruling covers only a standing woman, who strains, or a sitting woman too.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if the woman was sitting, what would רבי שמעון say? Maybe he was strict only when she was standing, because then she must strain, but not when she was sitting. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a dilemma about how far רבי שמעון's strict view reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A standing woman must strain to urinate, so the blood may well have come from her womb. That would explain רבי שמעון's strictness. A sitting woman does not strain, so perhaps even רבי שמעון would agree she is pure. The question is whether his ruling depends on her position.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open dilemma)
Or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה יוֹשֶׁבֶת, מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: If the woman was sitting, what would Rabbi Shimon say?
When Rabbi Shimon ruled, was it about a standing woman,
who generally has to strain,
but if she was sitting, not?
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the reach of רבי שמעון's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי שמעון rules her טמאה even when she was sitting

steps.title: רבי שמעון rules her impure either way
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון rules she cannot blame a wound whether she was sitting or standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a ברייתא: if she was sitting, she may blame a wound, but if she was standing, she may not. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יוסי says that either way she may blame a wound. רבי שמעון says that either way she may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the dilemma with a ברייתא that sets out three views. רבי שמעון makes no difference between sitting and standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר splits the cases: sitting means pure, standing means impure. רבי יוסי is lenient in both, and רבי שמעון is strict in both. So רבי שמעון's strictness does not depend on straining, and the question is answered: לא שנא, there is no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: She may blame (the blood on a wound) and stay pure
She may not blame a wound, so she is impure

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
If she was sitting, she may blame a wound;
if she was standing, she may not blame a wound.
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ — תּוֹלָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: either way, she may blame a wound.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ — אֵינָהּ תּוֹלָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: either way, she may not blame a wound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma raised in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון rules her טמאה whether she was sitting or standing.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views about a woman alone. רבי מאיר: sitting means pure, standing means impure. רבי יוסי: pure either way. רבי שמעון: impure either way.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Here רבי מאיר is strict only for a standing woman alone, while in the man-and-woman case (step 20) he rules her pure.

steps.title: Does רבי שמעון stay strict when a man and a woman were both sitting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי שמעון's strict ruling covers a case of ספק ספקא: a man and a woman both sitting and urinating into the same basin.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if a man and a woman were sitting, what would רבי שמעון say? Maybe he was strict only for a standing woman, who strains, or for a sitting woman alone, where there is only one doubt. But where there are two doubts he would not be strict. Or maybe it makes no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about רבי שמעון. When a man and a woman were both sitting and blood is found, is she still טמאה according to him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases there was only one doubt: did the blood come from a wound or from her womb? Here there are two doubts: maybe it is the man's blood, and even if it is hers, maybe it is from a wound. The question is whether a ספק ספקא is enough to make רבי שמעון lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question the גמרא wants resolved)
A double doubt: two separate reasons the blood might not be from her womb
Literally 'the world presses her'; a standing woman generally has to strain

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 21. There the question was about a woman sitting alone (one doubt). Here a man is sitting with her, which adds a second doubt.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
A man and a woman who were sitting,
what would Rabbi Shimon say?
When Rabbi Shimon gave his strict ruling, was it only for
a standing woman, who generally has to strain,
and a sitting woman, where there is only one doubt,
but in a double doubt he did not say it,
phrases.notes: The two doubts: maybe it is the man's blood, and even if it is hers, maybe it is from a wound.

phrases.english: or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Steps 21-22: after showing רבי שמעון is strict for a sitting woman alone, the גמרא asks about the harder case of a man and a woman sitting together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי שמעון's strict ruling also apply when there is a ספק ספקא (man and woman both sitting)?

steps.title: רבי שמעון's own words show no difference between standing and sitting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from רבי שמעון's words in the משנה, 'blood is presumed to come from the woman,' that he is strict in every case, even a double doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: since רבי שמעון said 'the presumption of blood is that it comes from the woman,' it makes no difference whether they were standing or sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by looking at the exact words רבי שמעון used in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון gives a general reason: blood is presumed to come from the woman, because a man does not normally pass blood. That reason has nothing to do with whether they were standing or sitting. So the doubt about the man does not count, and she is טמאה even when both were sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: The presumption is that blood comes from the woman
A presumption the הלכה relies on unless there is clear reason otherwise

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, blood found where a man and a woman urinated is presumed to be hers, whether they were standing or sitting, even though it is a double doubt.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Since Rabbi Shimon said
'the presumption is that blood comes from the woman,'
phrases.notes: These are רבי שמעון's own words in our משנה.

phrases.english: there is no difference whether they are standing
and no difference whether they are sitting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון's wording sets up a general presumption that the blood is the woman's, so he is strict even with a ספק ספקא, standing or sitting.

steps.title: New משנה: a woman who lent her garment may blame the borrower
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a woman lent her garment to a נכרית or a נדה and later found a blood stain on it, she may attribute the stain to the borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she lent her garment to a gentile woman or to a נדה, she may blame the stain on her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about blood stains (כתמים). A woman finds a stain on a garment that someone else wore before her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נכרית or a נדה could have left the stain. Because there is another possible source, the owner does not have to assume the blood is hers, so she stays טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her menstrual state of טומאה
Attributes (she may 'hang' the stain on another source)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If she lent her garment
to a gentile woman or to a menstruating woman,
she may attribute the stain to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' הִשְׁאִילָה חֲלוּקָהּ לְנׇכְרִית אוֹ לְנִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of רבי שמעון ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who lent her garment to a נכרית or a נדה may attribute a later stain to the borrower and stays טהורה.

steps.title: Three women share one garment or bench: all are impure
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if three women wore one garment or sat on one bench and blood was found on it, all three are טמאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three women who wore one garment, or who sat on one bench, and blood was found on it: all of them are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: a stain on something used by several women, where any one of them could be the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last case, the owner could pin the stain on the borrower. Here each woman is just as likely as the others to be the one who bled. So none of them can blame the others, and all three are טמאות.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one doubtful stain makes only one woman טמאה. Since each woman might be the source, the משנה rules all three טמאות.

phrases.english: Three women who wore one garment,
or who sat on one bench,
and blood was found on it,
all of them are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a contrasting case: no clear outside source, so no one can blame another.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When three women shared a garment or bench and blood is found on it, all three are טמאות.

steps.title: No stain impurity on a stone bench or bathhouse bench
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה rules that if the women sat on a stone bench or a bathhouse bench and blood was found there, they are טהורות, because an item that cannot become impure cannot carry stains.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the three women sat on a stone bench or on a bathhouse bench and blood was found, רבי נחמיה says they are pure. He held that any item that cannot become impure also cannot receive the impurity of stains.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives an exception to the case just before it. If the bench is one that cannot become impure, רבי נחמיה says the blood found on it does not make the women טמאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stone items, and a bench attached to the floor of a bathhouse, cannot become טמא. רבי נחמיה says the rule of כתמים only applies to items that can become impure, so a stain on these benches means nothing. This limits the strict ruling in step 26 to benches and garments that can become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: A bench, here one built into a bathhouse
Blood stains, which can make a woman טמאה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי נחמיה, stain impurity only exists on items that can themselves become impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule gives a simple test for stains: first ask whether the item it was found on can become טמא at all.

phrases.english: If they sat on a stone bench
or on the bench of a bathhouse
phrases.notes: This bench is attached to the floor, so like stone, it cannot become impure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya rules them pure.
For Rabbi Nechemya would say:
Any item that cannot become impure
cannot receive stains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to step 26's ruling that all three women are טמאות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood found on an item that cannot become impure, such as a stone or bathhouse bench, does not make the women טמאות, according to רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: רב begins explaining the case of the gentile woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens, and רב starts to explain that the משנה's ruling about lending a garment applies to a specific case of a נכרית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא begins. רב says: the ruling is talking about a gentile woman...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts, and רב goes back to the משנה's first case, where a woman lent her garment to a נכרית. His statement continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the woman may blame the stain on the borrower. רב is beginning to define exactly what kind of נכרית case the משנה means. The rest of his explanation comes next.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav says: with regard to a gentile woman

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה has ended. The גמרא now goes back to the first case of the משנה (step 25) to explain it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב begins defining the case of the נכרית in the משנה. The details continue in the next part of the text.
